title: [YouPass Collect] - International Student Enrollment Trends 2002-2007
prompt: The graph below shows the number of students from the US, the UK and Australia who studied in universities in other countries from 2002 to 2007. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The line graph illustrates the number of students from the United States, the United Kingdom, and Australia who pursued their studies at universities in other countries between 2002 and 2007.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, the three countries exhibited distinct trends during this period, with the US showing a slight overall increase despite some fluctuations, the UK experiencing a steady decline, and Australia remaining completely stable. Throughout the timeframe, American students consistently represented the largest group studying abroad, while their Australian counterparts accounted for the smallest proportion.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Regarding the two countries with higher figures, in 2002, approximately 49,000 US students were studying overseas, which was significantly higher than the UK's figure of 30,000. The number of British students abroad then decreased consistently throughout the period, falling by 2,000 every two years on average, and ultimately reaching roughly 22,000 by 2007. Conversely, the US figures displayed a more fluctuating pattern, initially dropping to around 46,000 in 2004 before recovering to previous levels by 2006, and finally rising to 50,000 in the final year.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: With regard to Australia, the number of students studying in other countries stood at 10,000 in 2002, which was substantially lower than both the US and the UK. Remarkably, this figure remained completely unchanged throughout the entire six-year period, maintaining a constant level of 10,000 students annually.
